description: Claude Code's digitless tool-permission box (No / Yes, no row numbers) with the highlight on No, below user turns drawn with the same ❯ glyph, one of them starting 'Yes'. On the live original of this screen the model put `selected` on Yes in 4 of 6 runs, so the phone's cursor walk thought the highlight was already on Yes and pressed Enter, which chose No ('Interrupted'). classify() now reads `selected` off the last ❯ row, so this pins answer_style=cursor, selected=0 and the arrow keymap. The misread is flaky and this fictional copy rarely triggers it (the rows' trailing padding and wording both matter), so tests/test_cursor_select.py is what proves the override; this sample guards the shape. Fictional reconstruction of a live screen (tmux-rc, 2026-10-09).
